headline: Argentine Bonds Fall as Country Risk Exceeds 900 Points
summary: Argentine sovereign bonds declined by up to 3%, pushing the country risk indicator calculated by JP Morgan above 900 points.
why: Rising country risk indicators reflect investor concerns regarding Argentina's fiscal sustainability and economic stability.

impacts.name: Argentina
impacts.why: Sovereign bond prices are falling, increasing the country's risk premium.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Investors are pricing in higher default risk, leading to a sell-off in sovereign debt and a spike in risk premiums.
